_listen: One address or a list of them. Loopback only by default, because 127.0.0.1:11434 is what the ollama CLI assumes and it is the only address that is correct on every host. Deliberately NOT 0.0.0.0: the proxy has no authentication of its own, so anything that can reach the port can drive the models and read the prompts, and 0.0.0.0 exposes it on every network the host happens to be attached to -- including untrusted ones. To reach it from another machine, name that one interface's address explicitly rather than widening to 0.0.0.0. Since such an address is a property of the host and not of this project, set it in OLLAMA_PROXY_LISTEN (comma separated) instead of editing this file; the environment wins over the value here. List loopback first: a bind failure on one address is a warning rather than fatal, so local use keeps working when an on-demand interface such as a VPN is down.
_backends: One server per KV cache type, because OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE is read once at server start and has no per-request override. Every other setting that matters (num_ctx, num_predict, temperature) can be set per request, so it needs no server of its own. Only f16 is listed now, and start-stack.ps1 starts only that one: nothing routes to q8_0 (see _routes), so a second server was costing a process and six seconds of startup to receive no requests. To route a model to q8_0 again, start with -WithQ8 and add "q8": "http://127.0.0.1:11435" back here; a route naming a backend that is not listed fails validation at startup rather than at request time. MEASURING does not need this entry -- bench-model.ps1 talks to the backend ports directly, so -WithQ8 on its own is enough.
_backends_llama: bonsai is not ollama at all: it is a llama-server in router mode (--models-preset), because the Ternary Bonsai GGUFs use quant types (PQ2_0, Q2_0_g64) that only PrismML's llama.cpp fork implements, and ollama bundles upstream llama.cpp. The router loads a model on its first request and unloads it on POST /models/unload, which is what the proxy's eviction uses, so switching between an ollama model and a bonsai one frees VRAM in both directions exactly as switching between q8 and f16 did. It speaks only the OpenAI API: clients reach it through /v1/chat/completions, the proxy translates its model list into /api/tags, /api/ps and /v1/models, and any other /api/* call naming a bonsai model gets a 400 saying so. start-stack.ps1 starts it when LLAMA_SERVER_EXE and LLAMA_SERVER_PRESETS are set; the preset file (model paths, context, sampling) is host-specific and lives outside this repo. Measured 2026-09-21 on ternary-bonsai-2-27b at ctx 32768: ~63 tok/s eval, cold load 4.7 s, and it fills the GPU, so it cannot share VRAM with any ollama model.
_default: f16, now on measured merit rather than only as a safety fallback. The original reason was a hard constraint: q8_0 quantises KV in blocks of 32, which must divide the model's V head dimension, and kimi-linear (n_embd_head_v=72) could never load on it. kimi-linear was deleted 2026-09-04 and every model now owned has head_v 64/128/256, so the constraint no longer binds anything -- but f16 also won every measurement below, so the default stands on its own.
_routes: Longest matching prefix wins, so 'gemma4' would cover 'gemma4:12b'. Deliberately EMPTY: re-measured 2026-09-04 on ollama 0.33.2 (10GB RTX 3080, ctx 16384, num_parallel 1, temperature 0, eval tok/s, f16 vs q8) and f16 won on every model owned. lfm2.5:8b 311.5 vs 111.8 (-64%); nemotron-3.5-lightning:30b-a3b 37.4 vs 11.7 (-69%); north-mini-code-1.0 33.0 vs 30.3 (-8%); ministral-3:14b 12.1 vs 12.3 (+1.4%, under the 3% bar); qwen3.8:27b 8.0 vs 6.2 (-23%).
_routes_history: The August entries were gemma4 -> q8 (53.9 -> 62.9) and qwen3-coder -> q8 (29.6 -> 31.0), both measured on an earlier ollama. Both models were deleted 2026-09-04, so the routes went with them. Those numbers now contradict every 2026-09-04 measurement, so if either model is pulled again, re-measure with bench-model.ps1 rather than restoring the old route -- and see _q8_instability before trusting a single run.
_routes_bonsai: The one route is not a KV-cache choice: ternary-bonsai models exist only on the llama-server backend, so they must be routed there by name. The prefix covers every preset whose id starts with it. Preset ids use dashes, not ollama's name:tag, because the router upper-cases whatever follows a colon (it reads it as a Hugging Face quant tag), so 'ternary-bonsai-2:27b' would have been listed as ':27B' and then not found under the name clients were given.
_q8_instability: q8 is not merely slower here, it is non-reproducible. nemotron-3.5-lightning:30b-a3b measured 11.7 tok/s with f16 benchmarked first and 4.1 tok/s (runs of 2.8 and 5.4) with q8 benchmarked first, a 4x swing for the same model, context and backend. f16 returned 37.4 in BOTH orders (37.1-37.8, then 37.7/37.2). Measurement order was tested explicitly and ruled out as the cause: q8 got worse when it went first, not better. Treat any single q8 measurement as unreliable; require a repeat in both orders before routing to it.
_options: Merged into a model-bearing request when the client omits the key; an explicit client value always wins. Matched by the same longest prefix as routes. num_parallel=1 at server start remains the big win (gemma4 28.1 -> 62.9). Halving num_ctx buys nothing for a model that already fits entirely (gemma4 62.9 at 16384 vs 62.8 at 8192) -- but it is worth a lot for one that sits just over the VRAM line, which is what the ministral-3:14b entry below was.
_options_ministral: ministral-3:14b is 8.5GB of weights against 8.9GiB of usable VRAM, so KV cache decides how much spills to CPU. Measured on f16 2026-09-04: ctx 16384 -> 12.1 tok/s, ctx 8192 -> 18.4 (+52%), ctx 4096 -> 24.1 (+99%). The curve never flattens, meaning the model never fully fits at any useful context; 8192 is chosen as the knee that keeps a usable window rather than the fastest number. This is only a DEFAULT: a client that sends its own num_ctx still gets it. Note this is a per-tag prefix, so ministral-3:3b and :8b (which fit) are untouched.
_options_v1_blind: EMPTIED 2026-09-21, because options never reach the clients that matter: ollama's /v1/chat/completions ignores an options object entirely (sent num_ctx 4096 and 12288, both loaded at the server default). The agent client here speaks /v1, so the 8192 ministral cap above only ever applied to native /api callers, and that client was really getting 16384 while its config said 8192. On /v1 the only per-model context knob is the tag itself (PARAMETER num_ctx in the modelfile). So context is now set by the server default (32768, see ollama-serve-awake.ps1) plus a tag for the exception: ministral-3:14b-16k, measured 10.4 tok/s at 16384 vs 7.9 at 32768 on 2026-09-21. The old entries would also have been actively wrong now: the 'ministral-3:14b' prefix matches 'ministral-3:14b-16k' and would have forced 8192 onto /api callers of a tag that exists to pin 16384. The mechanism stays for /api-only tuning; any entry added here must be checked against the longer tags its prefix swallows.
_defaults: Same merge and the same longest-prefix match as options, but for fields beside the options object rather than inside it. think is one: it is top-level in the ollama request, so options cannot reach it. An empty prefix would match every model; it is no longer used here, because the one field defaulted is not safe on every model.
_defaults_think: think does NOT control whether the model reasons -- only whether ollama parses the reasoning into its own field. Re-measured 2026-09-09 on ollama 0.33.2 with '17 * 23' at temperature 0. lfm2.5:8b spent exactly 105 eval tokens in all three cases: no think field -> <think>...</think> sitting inline in response; think:false -> byte-identical to omitting it; think:true -> 305 chars in the separate thinking field and a clean response. So the old blanket think:false bought nothing -- no token saving, no cleaner answer -- and the budget argument it was written on does not hold for the models owned now. It is replaced by think:true on the models that can honor it, which is the only setting that keeps the tags out of response.
_defaults_think_capability: think:true CANNOT be blanket: ministral-3:14b returns HTTP 400 '"ministral-3:14b" does not support thinking'. The gate is the model's advertised capability, so the prefixes below are exactly the models whose 'ollama show' lists thinking -- lfm2.5, nemotron-3.5-lightning, north-mini-code-1.0, qwen3.6, qwen3.8. ministral-3 is the one model here without it and is deliberately absent. Enumerate the model list rather than the families you remember: qwen3.6:35b-a3b-coding was missed on the first pass because 'ollama list' was read only as far as the first few entries, and a thinking model with no prefix here silently leaks its tags into response. Re-check with 'ollama show <model>' before adding a prefix; a new model that cannot think will 400 on every request if it is added by mistake.
_defaults_v1_quirk: REVERSED 2026-09-09: injecting reasoning_effort:none was actively harmful and has been removed. On /v1/chat/completions ollama already separates reasoning by default (lfm2.5:8b: 305 chars in message.reasoning, clean content). Sending reasoning_effort:none does not stop the reasoning -- it stops ollama PARSING it, so the <think></think> tags leak into content instead, at identical token cost. Isolated on lfm2.5:8b: baseline clean, think:false clean (the /v1 endpoint ignores think, as previously recorded), reasoning_effort:none -> inline leak, both -> inline leak. The earlier qwen3.6:35b-a3b result that motivated it could not be re-tested; that model was deleted 2026-09-04.
_exclusive_defaults: think and reasoning_effort are the SAME switch on the two endpoints ollama exposes, so a client that pins either one is stating its intent and must not get the other defaulted against it. exclusive_defaults lists field-name groups: if a request already contains any member, none of the group's defaults are injected. Still earns its place with only think defaulted: a client that sends reasoning_effort must not also get think injected behind it.
